archetype: working rural ranchstead with a legible dwelling core, livestock and feed functions, equipment and utility support, fenced outdoor working areas, service circulation and a coherent long-abandonment ruin story
ground_program: primary ranch dwelling presents a recognizable front or side domestic entrance with porch, mudroom or sheltered threshold before entering living space rather than opening directly into agricultural service areas
domestic core includes differentiated kitchen, dining, living, sleeping and sanitation spaces sized and furnished as a modest rural residence rather than repeated generic rooms
mudroom or utility transition links the dwelling to exterior work circulation and provides credible storage for boots, tools, protective clothing and daily ranch equipment
detached or attached barn provides a clear livestock/feed program with stalls or pens, feed storage, tack or equipment storage and at least one vehicle- or livestock-scale access opening
one workshop, machinery shed or service bay supports repair and storage of ranch equipment and remains distinguishable from the barn through floor plan, access and fixtures

exterior working program includes fenced paddock or corral space, gates, loading or handling area, trough or water point and a route tying these areas to the barn without forcing livestock through domestic space
feed, hay or bulk-storage areas are positioned for direct service access and maintain believable separation from dwelling interiors, sanitation and ignition-prone workshop functions
waste, drainage, water supply and utility features are placed as functional parts of the site rather than decorative isolated blocks
foundation edges, porch steps, yard grading, tracks, drainage and fence lines seat the ranch into surrounding terrain without a single oversized artificial platform
upper_program: where the dwelling includes an upper or loft level, it contains sleeping, storage or small work rooms connected by a supported stair with usable landings and uninterrupted player headroom
barn lofts or elevated hay storage must be structurally supported, accessible by believable stairs, ladder-equivalent route or hoist arrangement and remain physically related to feed handling below
roof volumes differentiate dwelling, barn, workshop and utility structures so the ranch reads as an accumulated working site rather than one monolithic building
upper windows, dormers, vents and loft openings correspond to real interior spaces and agricultural ventilation needs rather than pasted facade decoration
chimney, flue, water, electrical and mechanical routes align with the rooms or equipment they serve and remain maintainable from surviving circulation
no elevated floor, balcony, loft or roof fragment may remain unsupported in either the clean master or derived damage state
circulation: residents can move between dwelling entrance, kitchen, mudroom, yard and principal work buildings without passing through livestock stalls or machinery hazards as the only route
livestock circulation connects paddock or corral, handling gate, barn and loading edge through openings sized for the represented animals and does not require passage through the dwelling
service vehicles can reach workshop, feed storage and barn service edges from an exterior track or yard without crossing the principal domestic porch or fenced animal holding area unnecessarily
feed and equipment handling routes remain short and direct between storage, barn and exterior work areas while preserving a distinguishable domestic zone
every occupied upper or loft level retains a physically supported player-scale route back to grade
damage variants must preserve at least one complete dwelling-to-yard-to-barn route and one viable route between the principal livestock area and surviving shelter
damage_constraints: the damaged derivative must remain immediately recognizable as a ranchstead through the surviving dwelling, barn, fences or corrals, feed/equipment areas and working-yard relationships rather than becoming a generic ruined farmhouse

favor long-term roof failure, rot, weather exposure, sagging or breached barn walls, collapsed fence sections, overgrowth, localized fire or equipment damage and gradual foundation distress over repeated rectangular deletion masks
major structural failure should affect one coherent portion of the ranch at a time and preserve gravity-consistent debris, supported surviving walls and understandable load paths
where roofs, lofts or floors fail, associated partitions, doors, glazing, fixtures, hay/feed storage and equipment must fail consistently so unsupported fragments do not float
preserve enough domestic room identity and agricultural infrastructure for the former household-and-ranch workflow to remain inferable during exploration
fences may be broken and gates jammed or missing, but surviving alignments must still reveal paddock, corral and livestock movement patterns
barn, workshop, feed storage and utility damage may expose their interiors but must preserve their distinct functions and spatial relationship to the working yard
derive damaged, occupied or contaminated variants only from this immutable clean master

required_manual_checks: the structure reads immediately as a working ranchstead rather than a generic farmhouse, suburban house, roadside business or decorative barn
dwelling, barn, livestock handling, feed storage, workshop or equipment support and fenced working areas form a believable rural production program
domestic, livestock and vehicle/service circulation remain distinguishable and do not depend on implausible shortcuts through bedrooms, stalls or machinery bays
barn stalls, feed areas, gates, corrals, troughs and service openings are dimensioned and connected as functional agricultural spaces rather than scenery
stairs, loft access and elevated storage are structurally supported and provide usable player-scale clearance where ordinary movement is intended
the decay story reads as prolonged abandonment and weathering with localized failures rather than arbitrary missing cubes
at least one dwelling-to-yard-to-barn route and one livestock-area-to-shelter route survive the damaged state
the ranch meets surrounding grade through believable tracks, yard drainage, porch/foundation transitions, fence lines and paddock edges without floating structures or buried access
